TOGETHER WITH BROADWAY IN BOSTON

You’re invited to the party of the summer

🥂🎉 Dress code: Roaring 20’s. The vibe: watching the opulent world of Jay Gatsby coming to life on the stage. Direct from Broadway, the Tony Award®-winning musical “The Great Gatsby” arrives at Citizens Opera House July 7–19 with all the lavish parties, complicated romance, and Jazz-Age-drama you loved about the book –– now with an irresistible score. Consider this your green light to grab tickets, old sport.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe.

🍻 PSA: You can cheers your beers for another hour! FINALLY: Nearly 200 bars across Boston have been approved to extend last call into the wee hours of the morning through July. A whopping ~130 of them are open ’till 3 a.m., with more to come on a rolling basis. See the full list of bars here. But with the way the Tartan Army is draining the city’s beer reserves, these bars better get ready for the long nights ahead. Just remember: the T will still only be running until 2 a.m. on match days …

⛴️ Save the Harbor is about to be your “friend with a boat.” Imagine: Golden hour views on the horizon, wind in your hair, and … no dimes dropped? Where do we sign?! You can now take a handful of free cruises around the harbor this summer, thanks to the folks at Save the Harbor. Wanna make a day out of it? Book one of the Sunday cruises to Spectacle Island for beach vibes, hiking, and more. But make sure to mark your calendars — registration opens three weeks before the date!

🍦 Boston’s favorite sweet spots are scooping for duty. Let’s plan out your next ice cream crawl now: Starting June 20, L.A. Burdick’s Brookline location will be slinging scoops, and the flavor lineup looks GAS. Think: Apricot elderflower, honey caramel truffle, and moscato butter. Next, head to Fenway to try Matcha Maiko’s new mango sticky rice parfait. And for the palate cleanser, try this new limonada sherbet from Honeycomb, inspired by the popular tart and creamy Brazilian bev.

ONE LAST THING

RO! RO!

Image: Stan Grossfeld/The Boston Globe.

Watch out Tartans, there’s a new soccer army in town. Norway’s Viking Army is now taking over the city … well specifically, our escalators.

Enter: The Viking Row. This is a classic Norwegian soccer tradition where fans sit down, lean forward, and pull back like they’re rowing and chanting in perfect unison. So they started doing it in the most obvious of places: the escalators at TD Garden and South Station.

But whether it’s on an escalator, in the stadium stands, or on the streets of Boston, these fans look like a well-oiled machine. And the energy is not slowing down after Norway beat Iraq in their first World Cup match.

Boston’s reaction? HYPED. Someone commented: “This confirms what I had long suspected: the Vikings never left us and are alive and well.”

Just plz don’t get your flags caught in the escalator …

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

🚣 Thanks for reading! OK, they can stay till the Head of the Charles.

💜 Special shoutout to today’s sponsor, Lexus Broadway in Boston, for supporting local journalism and reminding us that the best nights out usually involve a standing ovation. “The Great Gatsby” is also sponsored by Harvard Pilgrim Healthcare.

🏖️ The results are in: Most B-Siders have Ogunquit on their bucket list. And this cute Maine beach town is B-Side Certified (even in the fall). One echoed Kristi’s rec: “Piano bar is an absolute must!!”

title: Boston’s foodie hot list is here!
text:
It’s Monday, Boston.

🥧 On your marks … Get set … BAKE! Bake Club Boston’s sweet treat meet-up literally sells out like hotcakes. So they set aside a handful of spots to its great pie off on June 27 just for B-Siders. Translation: Grab your tickets ASAP!

👀 What’s on tap today:

Hello, 3 a.m. last calls!

Wet weather woes

SMH, Google Maps

Up first…

BEST OF THE BEST

The ultimate treat yo’self guide

Image: Anthony Adamick. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

The Globe literally ate with this list. Enter: “Best of the Best,” a.k.a. the Boston Globe’s guide to the greatest restaurants, shopping, events, and more around Boston. From bagels to breweries, all 300 of these spots were handpicked by journalists and trusted correspondents.

Here are some of our main takeaways:

🍦Cambridge’s ice cream game is ELITE. With beloved creameries like Honeycomb, Christina’s, Toscanini’s, and New City, it’s no surprise that most of the Globe’s ice cream picks have Cambridge digs. But more under-the-radar spots like Forge Baking Co. in Somerville, Delini Gelato in Roxbury, and The Ice Creamsmith in Dorchester, still got some love.

☕ Boston runs on more than just Dunkin’. Between coffee legends like George Howell, Caffe Vitoria, and 1369 Coffee House, we already know the region brews a mean cup. And plenty of newer cafes are making a splash, like Yego Coffee in Somerville and Little Wolf, a North Shore staple that just opened in Seaport last year.

🧁 These bake shops are B-Side Certified. Kelly LOVES the chocolate brioche from Michette, half moons from Lyndell’s, egg tarts from Ho Yuen, and pretty much every baklava from Yafa. Plus, don’t forget to go to Sofra and get Emily’s faves like the date turmeric cinnamon and almond rose cake.

🤑 These sub-$25 meals are no joke. Did you know there’s still a breakfast sandwich for under $5? Neither did we *adds Evergreen in JP to our Beli*. That might be the best deal we saw on this list, but these recs feature any and every cuisine you’re in the mood for, from baba ghanoush at Amba to arepas from Viva Mi Arepa.

🛍️ Our thrifting scene is small but mighty. We all know of Garment District, Goodwill, and SoWa … which BTW, did make the “Best of the Best.” But if you’re looking for niche finds, you’ll probably have luck at Blue Bandana Relics in Somerville, which gives Maine cabin vibes, and 40 South St. in JP for ’70s statement pieces. Another hidden gem: The Thrift Shop of Boston in Roslindale for clothes, kitchenware, vinyl, and the works.

🙌 Want more? You can go through all 25+ lists here.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH CAMBRIDGE TASTE

Social life feeling stale? Try this.

🍷 35+ reasons to camp out at University Park on June 17. Cambridge Taste is back with over 35 local restaurants sampling everything from sushi to wine to summer cocktails. Expect bites from Wusong Road’s innovative Asian cuisine, Barcelona Wine Bar’s Spanish small plates, Sumiao Hunan Kitchen’s fiery Hunan classics, plus Gufo’s handmade pasta, Fuji at Kendall’s fresh sashimi, Hourly Oyster’s raw bar, and so much more. All-inclusive tickets support local nonprofits. Get yours here.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Gretchen Ertl for The Boston Globe.

🍻 We’re one step closer to 3 a.m. PBRs, people! Remember that 3 a.m. last call proposal? House lawmakers unanimously approved it. The goal is two-fold: to cash in on the tourist boom this summer, and as a test to see what a last-call extension would look like. So what now? If it passes the Senate, cities and towns can opt to extend one hour past closing, from June 8 through July 31. They can also set their rules about which businesses can participate and designate public consumption zones. But bartenders are skeptical of how this will play out …

☔ This weekend weather is giving us 2025 flashbacks. In classic Boston fashion, we’re seeing gorgina weekdays and buckets of rain on the weekends. And it’s been going on like this for 13 weeks … in a ROW. Why? 1. A ~wavy~ jet stream bringing colder air from the north. And 2. The recent heat created more moisture in the atmosphere. So … will we see a dry June weekend? Probably … Hopefully … at least once?

🚗 Park in this lot lawn for the World Cup. We remember this drill from the Eras Tour all too well … With FIFA selling parking passes at $175 a pop, some local residents are offering their own lawns as alternatives. This practice is technically banned in Foxborough, but being only a mile away, some Walpole locals are taking full advantage of applying for stadium event licenses. One man plans to have 26 spots, priced at $100 per car. For all seven games, he could make more than $18,000!

🤩 Two hot new bombshells (hangouts) entered the villa (Boston). The Lawn on D just got a fresh green facelift and gave itself a new name, The Grove. Think: Lush greenery, cabanas, live music, and a menu packing poké bowls, watermelon frosés, and s’mores martinis. In the mood for carbs on the go? Curb your pasta cravings FAST at the Presto Pasta window in the North End. Just pick your pasta shape, sauce, and toppings, and voila!

THINGS TO DO

Weekday plans

Image: Craig F. Walker/The Boston Globe.

🤠 Giddy up to your next girl dinner. Hunter’s new cowgirl dinner deal is what dreams are made of: Steak frites + your choice of side salad = $30. Only available on Mondays!

🏌️ Make Wednesdays for the women. Five Iron Golf is celebrating Women’s Golf Month with up to 90 minutes of free play for the ladies on Wednesdays all June.

💻 See if a four-day work week is worth it. That’s the topic of discussion at this Binge Thinking event on June 10, where an expert shares what’s really happening inside companies trying it.

🌹 Bask among the blooms. The Kelleher Rose Garden is *this close* to peak bloom. Perfect timing for its annual Rose Garden picnic party on June 10 — yes it’s free!

🏳️‍🌈 Werk it at the market. The Brighton Bazaar is throwing its first-ever LGBTQ+ themed Big Gay Bazaar on June 11. Expect drag, a Lady Gaga Tribute, 100+ curated LGBTQ+ vendors, and more!

🌴 Outwit, outplay, outlast. Yes, we’re talking about Survivor Aeronaut on June 12, where you and your pals can play epic Survivor-style challenges and puzzles (all over a beer, ofc).

⚽ Practice your olé, olé, olés. Friendly reminder that the FIFA Fan Festival kicks off June 12 at City Hall Plaza, a prime spot for catching a match.

🍸 Get a taste of these STUNNING spring cocktails.* 89 Charles’ intimate cocktail lounge just unveiled fresh martinis, seasonal sips, and zero-proof options alongside elevated bar bites. It’s the kind of place you’ll keep coming back to. Reserve here.

*This listing is presented in partnership with 89 Charles.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

⚽ The World Cup has arrived. Here’s where to watch.

The World Cup is in Boston, and Fenway FC is your headquarters until the Final on July 19. Time Out Market Boston and Cisco Brewers are streaming every match — group stage, knockouts, all of it — and they’re staying open late because soccer waits for no one.

Catch the action on big screens inside and out on The Green at 401 Park. Or if coastal New England vibes are more your speed, post up in Cisco’s beer garden for cold craft pours and mouthwatering bites. When you’re ready for dinner, MIDA’s Boylston Street patio, bartaco, Shy Bird’s dog-friendly terrace, and The Citizen’s sidewalk seats put you right in the thick of it. Don’t be shy, pull up a chair in The Fenway for the full 90!

ONE LAST THING

A DoorDash dilemma

Image: AP Photo/David Zalubowski. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

What would you do if 36 lunches showed up on your front porch? Well, this woman — and the rats that would sniff it out — had been getting misplaced deliveries for YEARS (literally everything from ice cream cake to a McDonald’s Coke).

Why, you may ask? Frumie L. Burns wrote for Brookline News how her address is nearly the same as Brigham and Women’s Hospital. But one was Brookline and the other was Boston. To make it worse, they were less than one mile away from each other. And Google Maps never got it right.

Frumie and her husband tried their best to redirect delivery drivers to the hospital. In many cases, the two would quickly bring it over themselves, especially if it was flowers.

It got so bad that the couple even tried to change their address officially. But finally, Frumie’s husband wrote a lengthy complaint to Google Maps and DoorDash … and so far, it’s been a few weeks without a wrong delivery. Fingers crossed!

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

🥤 Thanks for reading! To all the BW nurses who never got their lunch order … it’s probably at Frumie’s.

💜 Special shoutout to today’s sponsor, Cambridge Taste, for supporting local journalism and giving us the gift of adult recess (and a social life) season after season.

🦞 The results are in: Wow, most of you got our pop quiz question right! The first (recorded) lobster roll was served at a Connecticut restaurant in the 1920s. “Lobster had the most extreme glow-up,” one of you said. She really did that.

title: Diva down on the Green Line
text:
It’s Thursday, Boston.

🐘 Tired: Somerville turkeys. Wired: Back Bay elephants. TBH,100 life-sized elephants were not on our bingo card …

👀 What’s on tap today:

Hottie alert

$69 omakase

Queen Maye’s preseason

Up first…

TRANSPORTATION

Green Liners are taking an L

Images: Pat Greenhouse/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Fire up the duck boats shuttle buses! ‘Cause we’re in for a BIG Green Line shutdown from Aug. 8-16 …

Here’s what to know:

🤔 Why is this happening again? The MBTA’s goal is two-fold: improve accessibility (we’ll dig into this in a sec) and replace the signal system, which should prevent T traffic and ultimately be more reliable in the long run.

⚒️ Back to that accessibility goal: Apparently, many Green Line stations were built before the Americans with Disabilities Act. So it’s time for some much-needed upgrades to a bunch of above-ground C branch stops on Beacon Street (think: sloped walkways, bigger/higher platforms).

🚃 OK, here’s the breakdown of branch shutdowns:

B branch: Gov. Center and Babcock Street is OOO. Your alts: Take the shuttle between Babcock Street and Back Bay (then get on the Orange), or ride the 57 fare-free. One bright side: You can ride from Babcock Street to BC for free.

C branch: No service from Gov. Center allllllllll the way to Cleveland Circle … There’ll be shuttles from Cleveland Circle to Back Bay, BUT they’ll skip St. Mary’s Street, Kent Street, and Brandon Hall.

D branch: Diva down from North Station to Kenmore. You’ll be shuttlin’, too, to Back Bay. Like the B, you can hop on the D from Kenmore outbound, at no charge.

E branch: Say goodbye to North Station to Heath Street. The 39 bus will be your bestie for getting to Back Bay (and the MBTA is beefing up the number of buses on the route).

🚨 Warning: Our spidey senses suspect Back Bay station on the Orange Line might be slammed.

😬 Friendly reminder: Symphony will still be closed after this … till 2029.

♿ Need accessible T service? There are vans between Copley and North Station.

🙏 Your white knight might be the Worcester commuter rail. Ride it fare-free between South Station, Back Bay, and Lansdowne. If you go beyond Lansdowne or you’re taking any other line, you’ll have to cough up the normal fares.

😓 Want more info? Here’s the deets.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Pat Greenhouse/The Boston Globe.

🥵 Annnnd we’re back with another ~heat advisory~. Temps are slated to soar into the high 80s today, but with the raging humidity, it’ll feel more like the high 90s. Plus, we’ll likely see some heavier storms on Friday and Saturday, coupled with some strong winds. BUT we shouldn’t see any flash floods this time *fingers crossed*. You know the deal: Here’s the map of the city’s cooling resources (yes, indoor ones, too!).

🧑‍🍳 There’s a new BPL chef in town. Meet Suman Shah, a.k.a. the new chef-in-residence at the Roxbury branch nutrition lab. In case you’re new here, this residency program brings in professional chefs to host community culinary classes, demos, 1:1 seshes, even menu planning. Her goals? Expand the BPL’s cooking programs (keep your eyes peeled here for future events), host cultural food convos, and help locals build simpler, healthier meals. Note: If you see a spot for any classes, snag it! They fill up fast.

✈️ JetBlue wants your fall trip to make it out of the group chat. PSA: They’re offering STEALS on select one-way flights this fall, both within the U.S. and to Europe — and they end TODAY. We’re talkin’ $129 to San Diego, $184 to Aruba, and if you want a cheaper (but still gorg) New England getaway, try this $59 flight to Presque Isle, Maine. You can also snag sub-$300 one-way tickets to London and get to Dublin for $319 for most of October.

🍣 Sorry, did you say $69 omakase??? Enter: Jūni, a new omakase spot opening in Quincy on Aug. 6, with prices we can actually get behind. For just $69, you can get 12 courses with sashimi, hand roll ingredients, and more (peep the soy marinated tuna!). Started by Momi Nonmi chef Chris Chung, this spot’s shtick is that you get *everything* on one big ol’ platter (vs. waiting for the chef to give you each piece), and you can build and eat it however you want.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

Pilates 51 stories above Boston?

🏙️ Fit Scene Boston and View Boston are teaming up for another round of their Rooftop Wellness Series on Aug. 15. Join Boston Body Pilates Waterfront for a signature mat class with Boston Body founders, and a Boston skyline backdrop that will make the class fly by. Strength, stretch, and sculpt while you take in the breathtaking views, then explore wellness vendor activations, and grab a curated goodie bag. Check in starts at 9 a.m. Book here!

ONE LAST THING

Bakemas training camp

Image: Scott Eisen/Getty Images. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Shhh! Our show is on! Patriots QB Drake Maye may be back to work at training camp, but so is the Queen of New England.

Our fave Pats WAG Ann Michael Maye is BACK with some sweeeeet recipes, starting with these delish PB&J-swirled blondies from Sarah Fennel’s “Sweet Tooth” cookbook.

We actually lol’d at this user’s comment: “I’m kicking my feet thinking how Drake is going to have a couple of these after a big nutritious dinner.”

Ann Michael’s goal this month: Make a cookbook recipe at least once a week to share with us. <3

And fans in the comments are already itching for this year’s Bakemas, a.k.a. her December baking series. (We’re four months out … but same.)

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

🍪 Thanks for reading! We smell another Super Bowl appearance … and cookies.

🦪 The results are in: 49% of readers are slurpin’ oysters by the dozen. But a good chunk of B-Siders are not fans. One simply wrote: “It’s a gross rock.” (lol) Respectfully, you might be eating the wrong side …

title: Enter: Boston’s pop-up nightclub
text:
It’s Tuesday, Boston.

🎃 BREAKING: Dunkin’ is giving away FREE PSLs!!! Get yours between 2-6 p.m. TODAY ONLY (with a qualifying purchase, while supplies last). On your mark … get set … GO!

🥳 And a very, very happy b-day to B-Side Members Moe Buckley and Mia Matthews! We hope your PSL tastes *extra* cinnamon-y today.

👀 What’s on tap today:

Clancy case update

Encore workers’ strike

Hottie with rock-hard abs hands?

Up first…

SEPTEMBER FREEBIES

Athenaeum, a cappella, and Asian festivals

Image: Robert Torres. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

“Do you remember all the freebies of September?” — probs Earth, Wind & Fire if they wrote their banger today. So if you spent too much over Labor Day weekend, here are some free things to do this month that’ll give your wallet a breather.

Add these to your cal:

🏋️ Keep up your fitness routine. This is the last month of Seaport Sweat’s *killer* outdoor workout lineup, with pilates, zumba, vinyasa, and even Sweatapalooza, a fitness festival on Sept. 12. Want to be indoors? Hit the Boston Landing Fit Fest on Sept. 12 instead.

🍺 Dust off your lederhosen. Go HARD for Oktoberfest with seasonal beers, food specials, live tunes, and steinholding contests. Kick it off at Long Live Roxbury on Sept. 12, then Portico on Sept. 19 and Trillium from Sept. 19-20.

🏮 Stack your weekends with Asian festivals. First up: the Mid-Autumn Lantern Festival on Sept. 12 with lion dances, kung fu, and more. Then shop the Made in Boston Festival, an AAPI market in Somerville on Sept. 13. End with the Thai Market Festival in Harvard Square on Sept. 26, with street food, a beer garden, and art vendors.

🎨 Hone your brushwork. Make your own watercolor masterpiece at Boston’s Watercolor Painting Workshops. Spots are filling FAST, but there are still openings for Sept. 13 in Roxbury and Sept. 26 in Franklin Park. Go, go, GO!

🍻 Raise a glass for the end of summer. Cheers with your besties at Boston Harbor Distillery on the Greenway for the Young Bostonians Collective’s End-of-Summer Bash on Sept. 15, ft. yard games and prize giveaways. Note: You must register in advance!

📚 Roam the Athenaeum fo’ free. Yup, you can wander all 12 floors of the Boston Athenaeum at its Community Day open house on Sept. 19. See rare special-collection items, live performances, and gorg views of the city.

🤠 Giddy up for fall. Boston Landing is going full Western for its Fall Festival on Sept. 19. Think: BBQ, line dancing, wild reptiles, mini pumpkin decorating, and more.

🌽 Taste every corner of New England. This year’s Local Food Festival on the Greenway on Sept. 20 will have ~100 vendors serving up the region’s finest, from blueberry crisps to Mexican-style street corn. And don’t forget to stay for the seafood cooking competition and hourly cooking demos!

💃 Hit the club for five days straight. And by club, we mean Dewey Square Park. From Sept. 23-27, Let’s Dance Boston is taking over with different styles of dance every night, including salsa, hustle, and Lindy Hop. No partner or experience needed!

🎤 Watch “Pitch Perfect” IRL. Aca-believe it: Jam out to all genres, from barbershop and jazz to modern pop, at the Boston A Cappella Festival at the Riverstage at Herter Park on Sept. 26.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH BOSTON BALLET

Two ballets. Zero chance of being bored.

🩰🧑‍🩰 “Cacti” brings stomping, slapping, and drumming. “Vertical Road” brings hypnotic movement and existential questions. Together, they make a pretty compelling case for a night at the ballet. See two of Boston Ballet’s most acclaimed contemporary works at Citizens Opera House Sept. 10–20 before the program heads to Paris. Save $25 on select performances with code PASSIONATE.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP.

⚖️ The Lindsay Clancy case status: mistrial. After about 37 hours of deliberations, multiple notes saying the jury was deadlocked, and a failed last-ditch defense effort to remove a holdout juror, the judge declared a mistrial Friday. ICYMI, Clancy was on trial for three counts of first-degree murder for her children’s deaths. Now, what happens next is up to Plymouth DA Timothy Cruz. His options: 1. Retry her for the same charges. 2. Pursue lesser charges. 3. Go for a plea deal. 4. Decline to prosecute again. Stay tuned …

🎰 Encore workers are spending DAYS on the picket line. More than 1,300 casino employees (i.e. housekeepers, cooks, slot attendants) walked out on Sept. 4 over contract negotiations. The two unions representing them are pushing for higher wages that would align with rates of unionized hotels downtown. Plus, the workers claim that Encore wants to get rid of the previous contract’s job security protections and health care benefits. Meanwhile, Encore isn’t exactly the destination it’s promised to be.

🌲 Mo’ trees, mo’ problems. Residents, property owners, and developers keep cutting down trees … while the city is trying to grow more. Boston’s tree canopy — the branches and leaves that cover the ground and cool temps — grew by 0.5% from 2019 to 2024, a small change but more than the five years prior. But much of the city’s efforts were offset by people chopping them down for housing, views, safety, etc., since a large share of the canopy is on private property. Now, the city is looking for other ways to plant more.

☎️ Got a love Q? Phone a friend. Time Out Market is now home to the Tell-A-Booth, a *massive* phone booth where you can call and leave messages (no quarters needed!) for Meredith Goldstein, host of the Love Letters advice column and podcast. It launched at the BPL earlier this year, designed as a safe space to share your thoughts. Here’s how it works: Step inside and pick up the payphone to ask an anonymous question or ramble about relationships, and Meredith may feature it in a future column.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

⏯️ Give yourself a break already!

The Pause Festival is coming up on Sept. 19, and the panels are STAR-STUDDED. Hear from Jade Shenker of “Owning Manhattan,” Clarke Carraway of “Love Island USA,” VP of Brand Jazmyn Williams of The Honey Pot Co., and MORE. And don’t forget, your ticket includes a chicken Caesar wrap from Olivia’s Organics, plus hundreds of dollars in freebies like Glowbar and The Tox facials, merch, and Lowe’s doughnuts! Get your ticket for $20 off here.

ONE LAST THING

Sexiest man alive

Image: Stefanie Rocknak. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

“He’s a 10 but he’s always grabbing his Moby Dick in public.” That’s what one person commented about this Herman Melville statue.

There’s a new 7.5-foot bronze statue of the famous “Moby Dick” author in New Bedford — and, to put it simply, he’s HOT. He’s turning heads around town with his big dreamy eyes, luscious hair, a windswept beard, and one hand clutching the whale’s ribcage. I mean, LOOK at that hand. Let’s just say, he would do *numbers* on Hinge today.

Sculptor Stefanie Rocknak, who also did Boston’s Edgar Allan Poe statue, said those details weren’t even exaggerated. Apparently, he was known for being well-groomed and handsome, just as attractive as she made him look.

For those who want to see the baddie for themselves, Melville is standing tall outside of Seamen’s Bethel in New Bedford (walkable from the commuter rail stop btw). You can thank us later. 😉

— Written by Kelly Chan

🍿 Thanks for reading! If a Melville biopic comes out … we’re sat.

💜 Special shoutout to today’s sponsor, Boston Ballet, for supporting local journalism and proving that dance can come in all shapes, styles, and levels of jaw-dropping.

📲 The results are in: 74% of B-Siders support Harvard rolling out phone pouches. One reader even said, “Can I get one for my boyfriend?” Add this to your cart, girl.

title: The MBTA’s Gilmore Girls era
text:
Happy Friday, Boston!

⛴️ Set your alarms for a free ferry! Save the Harbor is dropping tickets at midnight on Sept. 13 for a free roundtrip ride to Spectacle Island on Oct. 4. Woo!

🥨 Party like it’s Oktober. We’re kicking off Oktoberfest season with Sam Adams Boston Brewery and Sam Adams Downtown Taproom! Tune into Saturday’s B-Side Member newsletter to snag a free pair of tickets — we’ve got two pairs for each event! Didn’t win? The first 50 Members can take 20% off.

Want in? Start a Membership for 50% off here. You just have to be the first to email us according to the directions. Prost!

👀 What’s on tap today:

Foliage forecast

The ultimate workout weekend

Boston’s karaoke king

Up first…

TRAVEL

$1 fall day trips make us holla

Image: John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Friendly reminder for our fellow Type A baddies: Commuter rail weekend passes are just $10, AND if you’re a monthly pass holder, you can bring one companion on weekend trips for just $1 each way through November (thanks, Gov. Healey!).

So we talked to our pals, our co-workers, and our team to map out four weekend-worthy autumnal adventures for you and bestie. Here’s where we’d go:

🧙 Salem, Mass.: I mean … duh. But fair warning: It’s gonna be packed come October. So head up this month to beat the spooky rush. Our game plan:

Fuel up at A&J King Artisan Bakers with fresh pastries and coffee.

Hit up the spooky staples like the “Bewitched” statue, the Ropes Mansion, the Witch House, and The House of the Seven Gables.

Explore the Peabody Essex Museum — it covers everything from witch trials to nature and science. This studio glass exhibit looks SICK.

Shop the city’s Haunted Happenings Marketplace for spooky trinkets and treats.

Cap off the night with freshly-baked cookies from Goodnight Fatty (obv).

🍎 Ayer + Harvard, Mass.: These quaint towns nestled in Nashoba Valley are loaded with rolling hills, fabulous foliage, and sweet treats galore. Our dream date looks something like this:

Grab a fresh apple fritter and coffee from Adams Donut Shop.

Fill a bag with fresh-picked apples at Doe Orchards.

Leaf peep along the Nashua River Rail Trail — you can walk or BYOB (bring your own bike!).

Step inside Amos Bronson Alcott’s utopian experiment at the Fruitlands Museum.

🍁 Ipswich, Mass.: You might not think beach + fall adds up to an ideal autumn outing. But this itinerary might change your tune:

Grab coffee and a breakfast sammie from Sandpiper Bakery.

Dig for vintage treasure at AnnTiques.

Pretend Castle Hill on the Crane Estate is your mansion for the day.

Enjoy an autumnal stroll along the gorgeous Crane Beach (just make sure to grab a pass!).

Pick apples, sip local wine, and say hi to cutie farm animals at Russell Orchards.

🧖 Newburyport, Mass.: She’s the queen of the downtown bop and shop. But Newburyport (and the surrounding area) is home to plenty of cozy fall excursions that go beyond the usual shmy:

Experience Skog & Stone Sauna Co.’s Finnish-style sauna on the beach on Plum Island.

Grab coffee and pastries at Middle Street Foods.

Uber to Cider Hill Farm (technically in Amesbury) for apple picking and cider doughnuts.

Take a fall hot girl walk through Maudslay State Park for epic leaf-peeping.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH SNOWBOUND EXPO

“Isn’t it a little early to be thinking about snow?”

❄️🎿 Respectfully, no. Snowbound Expo is already getting ready to bring the snow-sport community together Nov. 14–15 at Mohegan Sun. Come shop gear, get inspired by Olympians and athletes, watch some seriously unhinged tricks at the Rail Jam, and catch 60 looks on the Alpine runway. Then stick around for the Ice Bar and Saturday’s Après Party After Hours. For a limited time only, Early-Bird tickets are 50% off with code BSIDE.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe.

🍁 This foliage season is about to HIT. At least, compared to years past. Globe meteorologist Ken Mahan is expecting a good ol’, classic, vibrant New England fall with all the reds, oranges, and yellows of your dreams. ✍️ Lindsay Clancy’s attorney is doing the most to avoid a retrial. Kevin Reddington renewed a motion asking the judge to reconsider Clancy’s requests for a not-guilty finding, which can be granted when there’s not enough evidence to convict. He’s also trying to get her case dismissed entirely on double jeopardy grounds … except hung-jury mistrials typically don’t count toward double jeopardy. He argued that the judge could’ve done more about the lone holdout juror (who another juror called out for “disgusting” behavior during deliberations).

Poetry, pickleball, and pasta

The birthday party starts here

💦 Soooo … our wet weekends need to be wetter. We can’t believe we’re saying that either, but this is actually the city’s driest year on record. Boston has just under a foot of precipitation this year — nine inches less than average. title: Gen Z’s AI situationship ...
text:
It’s Thursday, Boston.

✈️ This woman NEEDS to be the next voice of Logan. If the contest winner doesn’t have a thick Boston accent, we’re rioting.

👀 What’s on tap today:

Reparations report got axed

MBTA’s biggest slowpoke

Utah 🤝 Fenway

Up first…

EDUCATION

AI is testing recent grads

Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Gen Z’s AI relationship status: It’s complicated. Demand for AI skills is up in Boston’s entry-level job market, but despite being some of AI’s most frequent and savvy users, recent grads aren’t loving it.

Here’s what to know:

📈 Local job listings are leaning *heavy* on AI skills. Mentions of AI *tripled* within a year on Indeed, and more than a third of junior-level roles now call for using AI tools for tasks like reports, slide decks, and even emails (it was only at ~10% last fall).

😠 Ironically, Gen Z is very pessimistic about AI. Yes, Gen Z does use AI tools more than any other adult age group (especially at work), but they’re also the most concerned about its impact on jobs.

👀 And we can’t blame them for thinking the worst … Demand for junior-level employees dropped 35% between 2023 and 2025. And careers that are most vulnerable to AI had steep entry-level cuts. That said, the rate of interns getting hired full-time rose this year, after low offer rates for the last five years. And employers are projected to hire more.

🎓 To get ahead, a whole lotta students are switching majors. Nearly 40% have changed or thought about changing their major, field, or courses because of AI. Not to mention, more AI majors are popping up at colleges and universities in the Boston area … *cough cough* Northeastern …

🍅 Put it all together, and you’ve got young grads throwing proverbial tomatoes. Remember when students booed pro-AI commencement speakers?

🤷 An unfortunate truth: The better at AI you are, the more valuable you’re considered at work (for now). We’re not just talking about prompting and asking questions. Employers value young people who can use it for bigger things like data analysis or coding models. And experts say that those who immerse themselves in the tech will probs move up the corporate ladder … and those who don’t might be at higher risk of getting laid off. Yikes.

🤔 Wanna dig deeper? Here’s the full Globe story.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH BRANDEIS UNIVERSITY

So…grad school?

🎓 Be honest, you’ve thought about it. Now, make a plan for it. Brandeis has master’s programs across business, policy, the sciences, and humanities — including highly ranked programs in public policy, finance, and business analytics. As a small R1 university, you’ll get wide-ranging research opportunities and a personalized academic experience, with internships in Boston, research, teaching, and career opportunities just minutes away. Join an upcoming virtual event to learn more (and get your application fee waived in the process) and apply by Oct. 15 for spring 2027 or Jan. 15 for fall 2027.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe.

❤️‍🩹 Postpartum mental health in Mass. might get a boost. Following the Lindsay Clancy trial, Gov. Maura Healey just pitched investing $2 million into the Welcome Family program, which sends nurses to visit and help new mothers after giving birth. They’d assist with things like breastfeeding, newborn care, mental health, and even caregiver referrals. For context, the program serves ~3,000 births per year (there are ~68,000 births/year in Mass.) — and currently receives no state funding but relies on federal dollars.

🫩 Say goodbye to one of Boston’s reparations reports … The City of Boston just scrapped it after one of the researchers was accused of factual errors and miscited credits in her own book on slavery. ICYMI: This report had been in the works for years to review the city’s history with slavery and its impacts, and evaluate potential reparations for Black Bostonians … and it was nearly three years overdue. City officials didn’t say if it’ll find another team for the report, but its $335K in funding will still be used for Boston’s Task Force on Reparations.

🚇 And MBTA slowpoke of the year is … Enter: the Pokey-Schleppie Awards. Transit Matters just put out its annual list of the slowest (Pokey) and most “bunched” (Schleppie) buses. The one that crawled the most? The SL4, which goes between South Station and Nubian Square, averaged at 6.09 mph and was somehow worse than the 1 bus (but not by much). Then there’s the 32, which ranked highest at 17.1% for bunching up (when buses aren’t spaced out so there’s huge waiting gaps). Congrats?

🧘 Get fit fo’ free this fall. Boston’s FREE Fall Fitness Series just kicked off this week! The city is hosting different workouts *every* day, including yoga, Zumba, and line dancing, across neighborhoods through Oct. 17 (except for Indigenous Peoples’ Day). Start off strong with a morning walking group, yoga, or Dancehall bootcamp (or all of the above!) on Sept. 19. See the full schedule here. Note: You must register for each.

Your pizza pilgrimage starts this weekend

City Hall Plaza is about to transform into the Boston Pizza Festival, loading in over 30 pizzerias (ovens included!) to sling slices for thousands of hungry guests. Advance tickets are still $10 for entry plus two slices, but that price climbs to $15 once the festival kicks off at 11 a.m., so lock it in now! Save $5 HERE with code BSIDE5.

Start an annual Membership here to get the discount code!

ONE LAST THING

Turn right on Pedroia

Image: Courtesy of EDGEhomes. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Ahhhh, Herriman, Utah, home of sprawling suburbs and … the Boston Red Sox?

Yep, this Utah city has a whole neighborhood filled with streets named after Red Sox players. See: Pedroia Street, Varitek Drive, Pesky Lane, and Eovaldi Avenue.

But like … why Utah??? Well, Brandon Parr, the project manager behind the development, is a lifelong Sox fan. When he proposed the project, he chose to honor a bunch of his fave players he grew up watching.

Fun fact: Quirky street names in the greater Salt Lake region aren’t hard to come by, with references to “The Lord of the Rings” (Gandalf Drive), Marvel (Hemsworth Way), and even “Wayne’s World” (Wayne’s World Drive).

Why didn’t Parr choose bigger legends like Williams or Ortiz? Apparently, there can’t be duplicate street names. Parr said that Yastrzemski Street might be on the table in the future … but it’d be a pain for mail carriers lol.

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

But luckily, Mass. has only seen a handful of cases this summer. While its source is still unclear, it’s been previously linked to contaminated food, particularly fresh produce, and water. For now, experts say to wash veggies and fruits very thoroughly (or cook them when possible), and avoid items like prewashed, bagged lettuce altogether.

title: How to make friends in Boston
text:
It’s Monday, Boston.

🚀 College student with a big idea? At Fetch’s Defeat the Odds Competition, students can win up to $30,000, connect with expert mentors, and pitch live at The Boston Globe’s Tech Innovation Summit on June 9. Apply for free and learn more here! Submit your application by March 20.

👀What’s on tap today:

New liquor license check

Your sign NOT to DoorDash

Put your headphones on!

Up first…

LIFESTYLE

How to make friends in Boston

Illustration: Gia Orsino

Here’s a puzzle: Boston is brimming with young people, yet most of us are lonely.

Case in point: Boston magazine’s Makena Gera recently realized she hadn’t organically made a new friend since college. So, she set out to investigate, and see if she could find friends in a seemingly hopeless place. Here’s what she found:

🧍 Yes, Boston has a loneliness problem. A recent study found that 43% of adults in Greater Boston reported feeling lonely — above the national average. Statewide, 25% of 18- to 24-year-olds say they “usually or always” feel isolated from others. The problem: “We are seeing a drastic change in society in terms of social ties. Especially after the COVID pandemic — we have Zoom, and everything is virtual, and we don’t know our neighbors anymore,” BU Professor Koichiro Shiba told Boston.

🤝 One solution: Friendship-making groups. In recent years, tons of local community-building groups have cropped up to get people meeting IRL, from run clubs to supper clubs to crafting meetups and more. “I noticed there were a lot of people like me who were looking for connection and didn’t know where to find it,” Boston Babes founder Rebekah King told Boston. Or, as Northeastern behavioral scientist Kristen Lee put it: “They give more opportunity and inroads that aren’t organically happening.”

👭 Some of them have an impressive track record. 28-year-old Luce Kelly basically found an entire friend group through Girlfriends Boston. She’s planning a birthday party with eight women she met through the group, all of whom she said she’d never have met otherwise. “They work in different sectors, or they live in different parts of the city or in other suburbs,” she told Boston. “There would have been no overlap whatsoever with a single one of the people who are my friends now.”

😬 But they don’t = automatic friendship. Over the winter, Gera set out to give the groups a try, attending painting classes, crafting meetups, dinners, and a comedy show. “I approached them all with mild apprehension, worried they would feel like networking — performative or contrived,” she wrote. Turns out, sometimes they were, but “the more groups I tried, the more natural it began to feel.” Eventually, she found her people among the Boston Drunken Knitwits.

💬 Ultimately, it’s up to you to shoot your shot. Gera’s takeaway: “The groups can put you in the room. They can hand you the conversation starters and seat you next to someone who also loves heated Pilates and has strong opinions about Yellowstone, but they can’t do the rest. You have to put in the work.” And if all else fails, at least you didn’t spend the evening doomscrolling.

🫂 Want to know more? You can read the whole story here.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH DISCOVERING KING TUT’S TOMB

​A night out … 3,000 years ago

🐍 Swap your usual weekend plans for something with a little more ✨lore ✨. Discovering King Tut’s Tomb drops you straight into the 1922 discovery of the Boy King’s burial chamber — complete with immersive recreations, exquisite handcrafted replicas, and an audio guide that walks you through the magic. Since the original artifacts will never leave Egypt again, this is as close to the real thing as you’re (probably) ever going to get. Grab your tickets and visit the NOW OPEN exhibit at The Saunders castle today! Boston Globe members save 15% off regular priced tickets with code: GLOBETUT.

BUY TICKETS

This offer is valid through Aug. 30 on Adult and Kids Admission tickets. To redeem, go to tutboston.com and use GLOBETUT in the voucher/gift voucher box.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

🍷 New liquor licenses, incoming! Last week, Boston doled out 13 new liquor licenses to restaurants in the South End, JP, East Boston, Roslindale, and West Roxbury. The new licenses are the latest batch to be handed out from the pool of 225 licenses the city created back in 2024 — an effort to make them more accessible and drive economic growth (they sell for up to $600,000). This round of recipients include Perch and Ula Cafe plus soon-to-open spots like Italian Express and Agosto. Check out the full list here.

🏀 Jayson Tatum is back in business. On Friday, the Celtics star finally made his return to the court at TD Garden 298 days after tearing his achilles in last year’s Eastern Conference Semifinals … a night we’d rather forget. Though he had some rust to shake off, Tatum looked good, sinking 15 points in 27 minutes. Not only is this great for JT, it’s a huge add for the C’s, who were already looking like legit contenders without him. Just listen to the crowd when he hits his first shot.

🥡 This is your sign NOT to DoorDash tonight. Ordering through third-party apps like DoorDash, Uber Eats, and GrubHub can cost diners a whopping 80% more than picking up takeout, and 600% more than cooking at home, per a recent report. Why? Most restaurants pay the apps a 15 to 30% fee on each order, which has forced some local spots to hike up delivery app prices to make up the difference. See: Stoked Pizza Company’s prices are at least 20% higher on the apps.

🍺 We see after-work drinks in your future. ‘Cause March 7 to 14 is Massachusetts Beer Week, an annual celebration where breweries across the state go all out to promote local craft beer. Interested? We’d recommend The Somerville Brewery Crawl. Between now and March 14, if you grab a stamp card at any participating spot and get it checked at Winter Hill Brewing, Portico Brewing, Aeronaut Brewing, and Remnant Brewing, you’ll win yourself a cute commemorative glass! What’s not to love?

THINGS TO DO

Weekday checklist

Image: Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images for The Recording Academy

🧠 Learn some local lore. Tonight, the Somerville Museum is hosting a Tavern Talk at Aeronaut Brewing about the infamous The Blizzard of ‘78. It’s like school, but way more fun, and with beer!

❄️ Say goodbye to winter … or wish it good riddance. Either way, Longwood’s lunchtime Winterfest on March 10 will have games, free coffee and cocoa, live music, and food trucks.

✍️ Genuinely enter a flow state. Trident’s writer’s group meets on the second Tuesday of every month (including March 10) to work on their projects using the pomodoro method.

🌃 Stargaze with strangers. Cambridge’s annual community astronomy night is March 11. You’ll explore the sky (and some free pizza) guided by folks from the Center for Astrophysics.

🎨 Make art after dark. March 12 is the ICA’s latest FREE nighttime art-making session. This week, you’ll learn about the Indigenous history of beading, and then try your hand at it. Grab tickets here!

🍝 Enter your mob wife era. Coppa will transform into an old-school red sauce joint à la “Goodfellas” on March 12. Expect an Italian prix fixe menu, black and white movies, and on-theme decor. Snag a res here.

🦢 Get your sad girl on. The Museum of Science is cosplaying as a Lana Del Rey concert on March 12. Iconic tribute singer Niki Luparelli will sing her hits accompanied by a 10-piece orchestra.

✂️ Join a crafty club. On March 12, Mayfly’s Stitch and Mend Club invites you to bring your crafty projects, start a new one, or just hang out and have some snacks.

ONE LAST THING

Know your airline etiquette

Image: Adobe. Illustration: Gia Orsino.

United passengers will have to make like Addison Rae … and put their headphones on.

Recently, the airline created a new rule that passengers can be kicked off of flights for listening to personal devices out loud. But according to Globe travel writer Christopher Muther, that’s just the tip of the airline etiquette iceberg,

Apparently, most airlines already say passengers can be booted for going barefoot or wearing “lewd” clothing. JetBlue even says it’ll have folks removed for “an offensive odor.” If only someone could have told her …

Since airlines seem to be tinkering with the rules, Muther floated a few suggestions: Passengers with middle seats should get both armrests, and people who recklessly recline their seats should be banned. Fair enough!

You can check all of his suggestions here.

— Written by Gia Orsino

🦶 Thanks for reading! While we’re here, should we just ban middle seats altogether?

💜 Special shoutout to today’s sponsor, Discovering King Tut’s Tomb, for supporting local journalism and bringing one of history’s greatest discoveries to Boston.

🍩 The results are in: Well, it was very close, but 35% of B-Siders said that Dunkin’ shouldn’t be able to sell drinks with 100+ grams of sugar. One reader disagreed: “It’s actually medically necessary for teenage girls to be drinking iced coffees with 100g of sugar. You can trust me, I was one of those girls.” Whatever you say!

title: Orange Line chose violence today
text:
It’s Thursday, Boston.

🥖 OMG. We need this baguette claw clip! Panera is giving away these adorable hair clips TODAY ONLY if you buy an Energy Refresher or Fresca (while supplies last, ofc).

🔥 Hot take: We think Boston’s cinnamon roll game is WEAK. Don’t agree? Prove us wrong by sharing where YOU get your fave cinnamon rolls in the city for our next B-Side Hotline. Fill out our form here!

New order on data centers

Top-tier mochi spots

The mattress that smiles back

Up first…

TRANSPORTATION

Here we go again …

Image: Carlin Stiehl for The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

No, you’re not having déjà vu. The Orange Line will be OOO (again) starting TODAY through Sept. 14. Just five days this time, bless.

Here’s what to know:

👋 Say goodbye to stops south of Back Bay. ‘Cause everything from Back Bay to Forest Hills will be shut down.

🛠️ The big work: Fixing up Ruggles and Jackson Square. It’s all part of the MBTA’s ongoing projects to make structural and accessibility improvements to both stations, like repairing platforms, stair walls, and bridges. They’ll also check off a couple other items on their to-do list, like signal upgrades.

🚌 Get pumped to reunite with your shuttle bus frenemies. Free, accessible shuttles will stop between Back Bay to Forest Hills. Traveling from Downtown Crossing to Forest Hills? Budget at least a half hour of travel time for your commute. We just hope they go in the right direction this time …

🚇 Your fastest option? The commuter rail. You can get from Forest Hills to Back Bay in ~10 minutes, and it’s fare-free during the shutdown. Plus, you can still hop off at Ruggles and South Station.

🫩 But brace yourself: This shutdown mayhem isn’t over. Parts of the Red Line, Green Line, and commuter rail will all be down the weekend of Sept. 19-20. More on that later, but in the meantime, you can read up on it here.

🤔 Want more info? Get all the deets here.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH NOBULL

Your workout called. It wants new shoes.

👟🔥 This is what your gym bag has been missing. Swing by NOBULL’s activation at The Pause Festival on Sept. 19 to try the Drive 2, NOBULL’s do-it-all training shoe, and even demo it during a workout. When you’re done doing the most, recover in the Recharge Slides — built for those sweet, sweet hours between training sessions. Plus: exclusive discount codes, giveaways and other onsite goodies. Consider it a little treat for your feet.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe.

🤖 Local data centers now need the people’s stamp of approval. Gov. Maura Healey signed an executive order requiring large data centers to get greenlit from the community before getting a permit. That means all new centers with a peak electricity demand of 25+ megawatts — one MW is enough to power 750-1,000 (!) homes — will have to file a community benefit agreement and a plan to meet eco criteria (think: water, air quality). Plus, they’ll have to fully fund their clean energy to support the center AND protect the neighboring environment.

🏀 It’s a GREAT day to be a women’s sports fan. Unrivaled, the 3-on-3 women’s basketball league, is opening its third season at TD Garden on Jan. 8 — marking its first-ever games in Boston. The league plans to play 10 nights at bigger venues nationwide after gaining HUGE crowds last season — and saw a women’s basketball record turnout with 21,490 fans in Philly. We’re seeing tickets starting at ~$55. And bonus: Your ticket gets you a seat for BOTH the 7:30 and 9 p.m. games that night.

😋 Boston’s got a serious case of mochi fever. That soft, stretchy rice dough is having a social media moment in the sun, and Globe food critic Devra First just blessed us with her top recs: 1. Crystal Bakery to customize your mochi with your dream toppings (i.e. strawbs, mango, matcha ice cream). 2. Kyōyo Haus, for soft-serve wrapped in mochi (their matcha soft serve slaps). 3. Golden Crust Bakery’s mochi breads. And 4. May’s Cake House for sweet sesame mochi balls coated in coconut, a.k.a., snowballs.

🍽️ We’re stealing this list of where the Globe’s food critic eats off the clock. Speaking of Devra … most of her picks are Asian comfort food (same). In Allston, hit up Kaju Tofu House for their sundubu jjigae and scallion pancakes, then Mountain House for dumplings and crab with sticky rice. But make sure to leave room for Meet Fresh’s shaved ice. Feeling dim sum? Ming’s Seafood. Thai? Mahaniyom (duh). And when Devra’s looking to switch it up, she’ll opt for Delfino in Rozzy and Prairie Fire in Brookline.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

A pizza lover’s DREAM is coming to Boston

🍕 Boston Pizza Festival is returning to City Hall Plaza Sept. 19 and 20, with 30+ pizzerias serving up slices. Taste pies from Sally’s Apizza, Quattro, Rossopomodoro at Eataly, and Pizza Taxi from Italy. Plus, watch a live pizza-making demo and sip Sam Adams beer, or Vinzo’s Wine, along the way. ONE LAST THING

Boston mattress makeovers?

A real $1 portrait of Kelly — but on a mattress. Image and illustration: Kelly Chan.

POV: Your trashed street mattress is smiling. And you can blame — or thank — Nick Shea.

Yes, the guy who draws $1 portraits on the Common has shifted his talents to a wee bit bigger canvas: dirty mattresses on the curb that were junked post-moving season.

“I do it because these things are just sitting, and they look gross and annoying,” he said to Boston.com. “So I’m like, what if I draw something on? At least people can look at it.”

Apparently, several of the mattresses have already been reported to 311 for removal … but in the meantime, we gotta admit they do look nicer, even when the markers smudge.

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

text:

Secret Spice Girl

SPORTS

The Pats are in their revenge era

Image: Robert F. Bukaty/AP. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Attention, Pats Nation: Church is now in session. Translation: Football season is BACK. The Pats kick off their season with a Super Bowl rematch against the Seattle Seahawks TONIGHT at 8:20 p.m. (Tbh, whoever created the NFL schedule is messy for that, but we respect it.)

So whether you’re in it for the blocks or Bakemas, here’s everything to know:

😬 ICYMI: Seattle gave us a capital “W” whooping in the Super Bowl. Like, scoring *zero* touchdowns in the first three quarters kind of whooping. Which was *especially* painful given our incredible Cinderella run. (Maybe those takes about our “easy schedule” were onto something …).

👀 Since then, the team’s made some BIG shifts this offseason. Namely, out: Kayshon Boutte and Stefon Diggs. In: A.J. Brown. New England traded two draft picks for Brown, a veteran wide receiver for the Eagles, and he’s STOKED to be here (he was a Pats fan as a kid!). They also gave a fat four-year, $135 million contract extension to Christian Gonzalez, making him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. Plus, we have 20+ new faces. Say hi!

👩‍❤️‍💋‍👨 Oh, and don’t forget the Vrabel drama … Head Coach Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini, formerly of The Athletic, caused quite the scandal when they were spotted hugging and sitting side-by-side in a pool (they’re both married). Russini resigned after the photos were leaked, and The Athletic just found their relationship to be in “clear violation” of its standards. And while Vrabel emerged pretty unscathed, the effects of the *situation* still linger.

😓 This season’s schedule looks a LOT tougher … If only it was as fun as their schedule announcement at Six Flags … Last season, the Pats had THE easiest schedule in 25 years, mostly because they were expected to be bad lol. Now, the first-place team is playing better teams and has a more challenging road to the SB.

💔 Speaking of … maybe don’t count on that Super Bowl appearance. At least, the Globe and Boston.com aren’t predicting they’ll win it all this year. A couple think they’ll make it back but … will likely lose to the L.A. Rams. PROVE THEM WRONG, DRAKE!

You can catch every game after at Legal Seafoods in the Seaport with $1 oysters or at High Street Place on Thursdays with a live DJ pre-kickoff. And of course, we’re tapped into Ann Michael Maye’s baking series, the social media team’s pranks, and the Mayes’ sitcom-style L.L. Bean ad (it’s actually hilarious).

🎶 Boston’s local music scene is falling flat. High costs, scarce affordable housing, and a shrinking pool of performance spaces aren’t making it easy on musicians here. In fact, next year’s spending plan takes a HUGE cut out of the Mayor’s Office of Art and Culture budget, which funds programs for local artists. title: Supper clubs are the new dinner parties
text:
Happy Friday, Boston!

💋 What’s Boston’s BEST first date spot? Is it cozy? Moody? Have lots of unobstructed exits? We’re cooking up a first date guide for our next B-Side hotline and want to hear from you! Drop your suggestions here!

👀What’s on tap today:

A picture perfect weekend

Get coffee with Mayor Wu

“Love Is Blind” in Boston

Up first…

GETTING OFFLINE

Meet us at supper club

Illustration: Gia Orsino

These days, Gen Z’s favorite club … is a supper club. As third spaces dwindle and traditional dinner parties are less accessible, supper clubs have become the hottest ticket in town.

Here’s what to know:

🍷 Supper clubs are the new dinner parties. “Everyone is dying to get around beautiful tables and meet new people,” said Aperitivo Society founder Maria Colalancia. But most 20-somethings don’t have the space, time, or friend group to host. Enter: Local clubs like Aperitivio, Drop Clock Club, and Pizza Le Beth, which do the heavy lifting for you by organizing ready-made, often aesthetically-pleasing dinner parties with good food and full tables. All you have to do is buy a ticket.

🍕 See: This cozy table at Pizza Le Beth. Co-founder Elizabeth Weihs and her husband, Peter, started their club after moving to Boston from Minnesota, where “everyone hung out at each other’s houses all the time,” she said. When they realized that was not the vibe in Boston, they took matters into their own hands: inviting strangers into their North End apartment for dinner. (Though they’ll be shifting their format to restaurants in the future after a snafu with the city.)

💬 Gen Z LOVES a hobby club. Andrew Roth, co-founder of IRL community marketing platform Offline, calls these types of gatherings “fourth spaces.” His thesis: After third spaces took a hit during the pandemic, young people shifted from gathering around places (think: gyms, cafes) to interests, creating a boom of hobby-based clubs like book clubs, run clubs, or craft groups. “Hosts are the new influencers,” he said.

🍴 The dinner table is a natural place to gather. Unlike clubs that center activities like running or crafting, sharing a meal immediately levels the playing field, since “everyone knows how to sit around a table and have dinner,” said Drop Clock founder Han (who doesn’t share her full name for anonymity). Colalancia agrees: “Just by introducing food into the situation, it breaks down a lot of barriers for people and makes people more comfortable.”

🤝 And small talk with strangers is good for the soul. Though friendship-making events are all the rage in Boston, Weihs’ goal for her dinners isn’t for folks to leave with a new bestie. It’s for everyone to spend a night feeling like they’re not alone. “You don’t need to be best friends with everyone, but there’s still a sense of community in knowing your neighbor,” she said. “It’s wild how much people need that.”

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe

☀️ The perfect weather weekend we’ve been waiting for is here! After eight straight weekends of chilly, rainy nonsense, Mother Nature is giving Bostonians the gorgina Saturday-Sunday combo we deserve: The forecast calls for dry, sunny weather in the mid-to-high 70s. Even better: Early projections show it’s only going to get nicer from there, with temps hitting the 80s on Monday and Tuesday. We’re not telling you to play hooky, but if you did … here are our fav places to swim around the city.

🎨 Latino arts have a new home in Boston. Introducing: La CASA, the largest Latino arts center in New England, which just opened in the South End. It’s the handiwork of local nonprofit Inquilinos Boricuas en Acción, which was established in the 1960s by local Puerto Ricans who were fighting displacement. Today, IBA works to help low-income families through affordable housing, education, financial empowerment, and arts education, and La CASA will become a new home for that work, as an event space and community hub. Here’s a peek inside!

☕ Mayor Michelle Wu wants to get coffee with YOU. Translation: Neighborhood coffee hours are BACK, where Wu and city staff head to Boston neighborhoods to chat directly with residents over a cup of Dunkin’ and doughnuts. Besides a chance to chat with the mayor IRL, the events will have lawn games, gift card giveaways, raffles, and free plants! It’s all kicking off in Elliot Norton Park on May 18, then Copley Square on May 27. More dates and neighborhoods will be coming soon, so stay tuned!

🍅 Big news for those who make artisanal jams their personality. The Copley Square Farmers Market, Boston’s largest farmers market, is back for the season in the newly-renovated Copley Square (which, BTW, may not be as terrible as the internet thought). The market will pop-up every Tuesday and Friday from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. through Nov. 24, with products from over three dozen Mass. farmers and food producers. Stop by today to catch special performances, food demos, and giveaways. Here’s a full vendor list.

THINGS TO DO

Weekend plans

🐼 Eat like a panda. Pandafest, one of the country’s biggest outdoor Asian food festivals, is in town all weekend long. Think: 80+ hand-picked food vendors serving panda-themed bites.

🌱 Become a plant parent. Emerald City Plant shop will be giving out free tropical plants on May 16 at the Mattapan BPL branch! They’re first-come, first-served, so get there early to claim your new baby.

💃 Salsa with fellow singles. If you’re single, chaotic, and love to dance, this chaotic singles salsa party on May 16 is for you. Bonus: Invite a dating app match and send them a screenshot for $5 tickets!

📚 Beef up your summer TBR pile. Meet iconic local authors, listen to panels, and shop from small book businesses at the fourth annual Greater Roxbury Book Fair on May 16.

🥳 Spread joy on the dance floor. Every month this summer, Roundhead Brewing Company’s JOY dance party is bringing good food, house music, and big energy. Check it out on May 16.

🚲 Join a pedal party. A.k.a. the city of Cambridge’s beginner-friendly group bike ride on May 16. The ride starts and ends at Joan Lorentz Park, bookended by a light breakfast and lunch. Bonus: It’s free!

🧘 Sip, savasana, and socialize. It’s all going down at NA bottle shop Dray on May 16: An all-levels yoga class, sound bath, and NA bev social.

🛍️ Shop your way though Inman Square. Delicious eats from local restaurants AND quirky maker markets? Say less! It’s all at the Inman Eats & Crafts fest on May 17.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

🏳️‍🌈 Step into Pride month the right way.

Strides for Action is celebrating 40 years of the Boston AIDS Walk on May 31 on the Common. Show up, get your steps in, and support a cause that matters — your participation keeps HIV prevention programs and LGBTQIA+ health services running across Mass. It’s free to register, the vibes are amazing, and you’ll probably make some friends. What more do you need? Sign up here.

ONE LAST THING

Love Is Blind … in Boston!

Image courtesy of Netflix. Illustration: Gia Orsino.

This is not a drill, B-Siders: “Love Is Blind” is finally coming to town! On Wednesday, Netflix announced the hit TV series’ 11th season will be set in Boston.

If you’ve been living under a rock, “Love Is Blind” is a reality dating show with a twist: couples meet, fall in love, and get engaged … all without seeing each other (until there’s a ring). Generally, it goes about as well as you can imagine.

Reality TV heads and longtime B-Siders know this has been in the works for a while (see: us announcing the casting call in 2024, and gossiping about filming locations in 2025). Since then, we’ve been waiting for the announcement, and after sitting through seasons in Minneapolis, Denver, and Ohio, we finally get our time.

The dates and details are TBD, but we know it’ll come out this fall. We’ll be counting down the days!

— Written by Gia Orsino and Emily Schario

👩‍❤️‍💋‍👨 Thanks for reading! Between this, “Love on the Spectrum,” and RHORI, we’re not sure what we did to deserve all this.

🥪 The results are in: 80% of B-Siders said they bring lunch instead of buying it. One reader said: “Third option: they make it for us.” Just curious … where do you work, and … are they hiring?

Boston’s climate plan

Fenway gets heated

Tell-a-Booth tales

Up first…

TELEPHONE TAG

Let’s do brunch, baby!

Illustration: Gia Orsino

What’s better than breakfast and lunch? BRUNCH! With Mother’s Day on the horizon, we asked the best brunch spots around Boston where they like to brunch. Spoiler: It’s diners.

Here’s what they said:

🥓Brassica Kitchen + Cafe wants a bite of Harry’s All American Breakfast. Despite running one of Boston’s best brunches, Brassica’s chef-owner Jeremy Kean isn’t a brunch guy. His first reaction to launching a brunch menu was literally “I’m not doing this.” (He’s since come around.) But he has a soft spot for Harry’s, a classic diner in Roslindale where “the service is … friendly and lovely.” His order: An omelet or a club sandwich.

🍔 Harry’s wants a bite of Rox Diner. Harry’s server Savion Allen-Harding wants brunch with a personal touch — food that “feels like they put their heart into it” and servers who treat you “like a regular human.” Luckily, he doesn’t have to go far to find it, just a mile down the road to Rox in West Roxbury. His picks: A burger or patty melt.

🍳 Rox Diner wants a bite of Deluxe Town Diner. How does Rox’s owner John Fortin judge a good brunch? “I can tell everything about the place by the eggs Benedict,” he said. Are they making their own hollandaise sauce? Is the muffin well-toasted? “If you do it right, then I’m guessing you do lots of things right on your brunch menu.” Let’s just say, he loves the eggs benny at Watertown’s Deluxe Town Diner (and Emily agrees).

🥞 Deluxe Town Diner wants a bite of Kelly’s Diner. It’s not surprising that Deluxe Town server Dina Marenco loves a retro diner (see: Deluxe Town’s tin can exterior and twinkle lights). But when she’s not at work, she’s at Kelly’s in Somerville, a legit 1950’s diner car with a bubblegum pink and teal counter that feels like a time capsule. As a self-proclaimed “pancake girl,” she always gets the pancake combo.

😋 Kelly’s Diner wants a bite of Jac’s Cafe. After managing Kelly’s for years, Ann (who declined to give her last name), is generally not a breakfast person: “I haven’t had eggs in over four years,” she said. Her one exception is Jac’s, a small Winthrop cafe with a family vibe and “the best” staff — especially “the girls at the counter.” With eggs off the table, her go-to order is French toast.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH THE FESTIVAL INTERNATIONAL DE JAZZ DE MONTREAL

A festival that won’t financially ruin you

🎶💸If Coachella had a more affordable, cultured cousin, it’d be this. From June 25 to July 4, the Festival International de Jazz de Montréal is bringing 350 concerts (most of them free) to the streets of downtown Montreal, just a day’s road trip from Boston. No overpriced weekend passes or Ticketmaster wars — just you and a lineup of artists like Lionel Richie, Earth, Wind & Fire, St. Vincent, Willow and more. This year also marks the 100th anniversary of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, so expect greatness (and probably some tribute performances). Start planning your trip today.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Erin Clark/The Boston Globe

🌎 Boston’s new Climate Action Plan is locked and loaded. Mayor Michelle Wu just unveiled the city’s new strategy to tackle climate change. The goal: Slash emissions in half by 2030 and hit carbon neutrality by 2050 (both of which are v ambitious given the lack of federal funding). The strategy: Target emissions from buildings and transportation by doubling down on existing emission-cutting programs and adding new ones. The plan: Help folks switch to electric stoves, discourage driving (including exploring congestion pricing!), and plant more trees, to name a few.

👑 This is who pulls the strings in Boston. Boston magazine just dropped its 2026 Power List of the city’s 150 most influential people. In spite of *recent events*, Mike Vrabel and Drake Maye earned the No. 1 spot for leading the Pats to a Super Bowl appearance. Gov. Maura Healey, Mayor Michelle Wu, Jaylen Brown, Elin Hilderbrand, and Fleet goalie Aerin Frankel, also cracked the top 50. Our fav pick? Queen of New England Ann Michael Maye, who nabbed 150. Check out the full list.

🔥 We’re going to the cottage Fenway this summer. Translation: Fenway just announced a “Heated Rivalry” night on Aug. 31! Think: A pre-game dance party, a cottage-themed transformation of the Sam Adams deck, trivia, themed food and drink, tickets sales supporting LGBTQ+ youth, and obviously, merch galore. All attendees will get either an Ilya or Shane-themed jersey, and VIP guests can snag this iconic hat. Tickets drop April 30 at 10 a.m. Grab them here.

😬 Boston’s biggest dining controversy: Foie gras. Animal rights activists have been making waves at swanky local restaurants for protesting the use of foie gras, a fattened duck or goose liver dish. According to the activists — who have protested at the likes of Pammy’s and Asta — the dish is inhumane, since it’s made by force feeding animals through a tube. Though they claim they got Pammy’s to nix the dish (Pammy’s didn’t confirm), their intense tactics have raised some eyebrows. Plus, many chefs argue they have the right to choose what they serve.

🌶 May 9: Boston Hot Sauce Festival, $12. The third annual Hot Sauce Festival is taking over The Foundry in Kendall Square with two Saturday sessions (12-4 p.m. and 4:30-8:30 p.m.). Expect global hot sauces from local makers, chef demos at the Spicy Food Lab, pepper-eating challenges, and fiery cocktails. B-Side Members save $5 on tickets. Register here.

ONE LAST THING

Tell-a-Booth tales

Image: Kelly Chan/Boston.com. Illustration: Gia Orsino.

This BPL phone booth has heard a lot of secrets. Over 1,000, to be exact.

Meet Tell-a-Booth, a bright red phone booth that’s been sitting in the BPL for two months, inviting patrons to step inside and spill their guts to Love Letters writer Meredith Goldstein … or just scream into the void (seriously).

Over 1,000 calls later, Goldstein shared her takeaways. Apparently, tourists leave the happiest voicemails (many of them slightly tipsy); college students are stressed out about feeling left behind (but they all feel the same way), and young people are searching for community (the good news: everyone is looking).

There’s a lot more where that came from. You can listen to her reflections in the newest episode of Love Letters.

title: This is “Heated Rivalry” IRL
text:
It’s Tuesday, Boston.

☕ And it’s National Coffee Day! Snag a FREE medium cup o’ joe from Dunkin’ with any purchase AND shop the new L.L. Bean collab collection, dropping TODAY at 10 a.m. We’re getting that tote like our lives depended on it.

🥳 Also, everyone sing HBD to Members Ida and Ayelet! We hope your day is complete with caffeine and retail therapy.

👀 What’s on tap today:

Boston v. Trump

Red Sox-Yankees rematch

MBTA-chella

Up first…

SPORTS

Puck around and find out

Image: Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

We’re feeling big-stick energy today. ‘Cause it’s the Bruins’ first game of the season, duh. Tune in TONIGHT at 8 p.m. to watch them play against the New York Rangers (boooo).

Here’s what to know before they take the ice:

🤦 First of all, we’ve got a timing issue. ‘Cause the Bruins game is at the *exact* same time as the Red Sox playoff game against the Yankees (more on that later). Classic. Get your remote ready to switch your channels FAST.

👏 OK, now let’s recap: We got to the playoffs last season!!! Which was a SHOCKER, to say the least. But first-year head coach Marco Sturm pulled through, with the team finishing fourth in the Atlantic Division before losing to the Buffalo Sabres in the first round … NGL, it sucked watching them lose every playoff game at TD Garden … But after the dumpster fire of a season the year before, we’re still calling this a win in our book.

💪 Big news: We finally have a captain (thank god). David Pastrnak — a.k.a. “Pasta,” the longest-tenured veteran with 12 seasons under his belt — officially got the “C” stitched onto his sweater this past weekend. In case you forgot, we didn’t have a captain at all last season, which hasn’t happened since ’01.

🫣 But heads up: You won’t see Charlie McAvoy … for a while. *Sigh* Our fave defenseman is suspended for six games after he took a BIG swing at Buffalo’s Zach Benson in the playoffs (yikes). His absence will be tough for a team that needs to start off strong in a v competitive Eastern Conference. Don’t expect to see him on the ice until Oct. 13 against the San Jose Sharks.

👀 Oh, and everybody say hi to JJ Peterka! Bruins brass traded two first-round picks for Peterka, a 24-year-old wing from the Utah Mammoth who’s got a need for speed. (Here’s a highlight reel for ya.) He’s had many skating bursts at 20+ miles an hour (!) AND averaged 26.6 goals per season over the last three years. And judging by his preseason performance, he def looks like a promising addition to the Bruins’ offense.

🙌 Keep an eye out for the youngsters. Particularly James Hagens, Fraser Minten, and Frederic Brunet. We know what to expect from seasoned players like Pasta and goalie Jeremy Swayman, but how these young guys grow as Bruins will be the real test this season. And Captain Pasta is making sure all the rookies feel welcome. <3

🏒 Wanna dig deeper? Read more about the Bruins here.

Injured in an accident? Know your options

🚗 An accident can change your life in seconds. If you’ve been injured in Massachusetts, you may be entitled to financial compensation. Whether you were in a car, riding a bike, in a rideshare, or hit by a truck, you may have options. Sokolove Law offers free legal consultations to help you understand what comes next. Call 1-800-CALL-JIM or get your free consultation today.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe.

☔ Mo’ rain, mo’ problems. As you could tell from your windows, this nor’easter raged across the state, with southeastern Mass. getting hit the hardest. Some towns got drenched in 7+ inches of rainfall, and 30+ communities clocked at least five. Sharon even got 10+ inches, one of the highest rainfall totals the region’s seen. Boston got less overall, though totals varied widely across neighborhoods: ~3 inches at Logan Airport, while JP got nearly six. The good news: All the rain will pretty much end by Tuesday.

⚖️ BREAKING: Trump, you just got served. Mayor Michelle Wu announced that the city is suing the Trump admin for withholding a whopping $20 million grant that was set to fund street-safety efforts in Roxbury (think: safer bike lanes, road maintenance, better bus service). The grant, which would’ve been used specifically for Melnea Cass Boulevard, Malcolm X Boulevard, and Warren Street, was revoked last September because the project included adding EV chargers. But the city says those chargers account for just 1% of the project’s total cost. Stay tuned …

⚾ The Red Sox are entering their revenge era. Practice your “Yankees Suck!” ‘cause the first round of the playoffs starts TONIGHT. ICYMI, the Sox lost to NY last year in the Wild Card Series. But after the comeback run they’ve had this summer, our fingers are crossed for this rematch. If we win two out of three games, we’ll secure a spot in the Division Series (the quarterfinals). Catch the games on NBC or at Fenway bars like The Bullpen, Bleacher Bar, and Game On! on Sept. 29-30 (and maybe Oct. 1).

💅 Now’s the time to glam up your bike gear. The Shiny Shop is hosting a *free* pop-up at Harvard’s Smith Campus Center, all in the name of community, micromobility (street safety for bikes, scooters, etc.), and art. On Wednesdays and Thursdays through Oct. 15, you can bring your helmet, bike basket, or any other commuter essentials that need a little love to a drop-in bedazzling sesh. Or you can learn new skills like fabric collaging on Oct. 1 and zinemaking on Oct. 8. See the full schedule here.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

100 years of flawless pizza

🍕Founded in 1926 in the North End, Regina Pizzeria was Boston’s first-ever pizza parlor. Today, a CENTURY later, their pies are still cooking in that OG brick oven, and they’ve kept the same formula. In 1956, the pizzeria started expanding throughout Greater Boston, but it’s always maintained its reputation for irresistible thin-crust pies and no gimmicks. 100 years is a rare milestone in the restaurant industry, so it’s cause for celebration at your nearest Regina’s.

ONE LAST THING

MBTA-chella

Images: Nina Corso; Lane Turner/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

The Boylston Squeal wasn’t the loudest thing on the T this weekend. Enter: “The MBTA Tour.”

Lazarus, a local college rock band, hosted a three-day T concert tour across the Green, Red, and Orange Lines this past weekend. The idea started after they performed on the Red Line back in July, and went viral.

And no, they didn’t get permission from the MBTA. They just planned out which stops to perform, found a spot on each train, and set up their equipment in less than 10 minutes. So naturally, a Green Line conductor shut them down Friday night … but they still kept the party going for the rest of the weekend on the other lines.

This either sounds like the best train ride of your life … or our worst nightmare.

— Written by Kelly Chan

🫩 Thanks for reading! Commuting with this + a nor’easter might’ve been our last straw.

Gas prices going up

NEW RESTAURANTS

Steak, soul, and soufflé

Image: David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Gia Orsino.

Fire up the Resy app, Boston. It’s time for another round of this month’s hottest restaurant openings. Per usual, Boston magazine and Boston.com have the roadmaps.

Here’s what’s cookin’:

🍷Beyond Proof, Jamaica Plain. Boston’s first zero proof cocktail bar and restaurant has touched down in JP. Inspired by her own sobriety and Gen Z’s shift away from drinking, owner Krista Kranyak reimagined her former restaurant, Ten Tables, into a trendy cocktail bar dressed head to toe in Millennial pink. On the menu: Mediterranean mezze and small plates, plus a lineup of $13 booze-free craft cocktails, other NA wines, beers, and liquor.

Things to try:

Abstinence in Bloom cocktail

Espresso martini

Fire roasted carrots with labneh and pistachio

🪩Uptown Social, South End/Roxbury. Southern soul food is coming to the South End. Formerly Bob the Chef’s, then Darryl’s Corner Bar & Kitchen, this storied venue was once described as “the Cheers of Black Boston.” Uptown Social aims to keep the music, community, and comfort food of Bob and Daryl’s, with a new elevated twist. Think: Chicken nuggets with caviar, fancy fish and grits, and live music brunch. Here’s a peek inside.

Things to try:

Chicken and waffles

Uptown nuggets with caviar

Rhythm and Spice cocktail

From the design to the menu, this new sibling to Mariel, Coquette, and My Girl subverts traditional steakhouse vibes (though FWIW, the prices don’t). The gorgeous, moody space covered in plush red fabric is hidden behind a bookshelf in Yvonne’s, speakeasy-style, with just 10 tables. Onion beignets

Wagyu petite filet

Cosmo highball cocktail

So far, the lineup is full of splashy international chains like China’s Molly Tea and ZhengXin Chicken Steak, or Toronto’s Fluffy Fluffy Dessert Cafe.

Jasmine tea at Molly Tea

Handrolls at Mi Nori Handroll

Soufflé from Fluffy Fluffy

🤤 Hungry for more? Check out Boston’s mag’s full roundup here, and Boston.com’s here.
